newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian minister says his society is "sick".
newsitem.headline: Indonesian minister says his society is "sick".

text.p: An Indonesian minister said on Thursday that recent riots in the multi-ethnic nation were a symptom of a sick society, the official Antara news agency reported.
"(Government) officials and the people are sick and unless we cure their sickness, national unity will disintegrate," Transmigration Minister Siswono Yudohusodo was quoted as saying.

Yudohusodo, known for his sometimes critical remarks on social issues, was commenting on the riots which have rocked capital Jakarta, West Java, East Java and West Kalimantan over the last six months.
In the latest incident, financial markets were briefly jolted by a gang turf war early on Thursday in which at least 10 people were detained in the central Jakarta district of Tanah Abang.
Yudohusodo said to cure the "sickness", laws must be obeyed, order and morality restored and government officials must become role models.

He said he regretted what he called the unethical and corrupt practices of some government officials when many of Indonesia's more than 200 million people continued to face problems of poverty, unemployment and social injustice.
Last week, an ethnic riot broke out in Sanggau Ledo district in West Kalimantan after a man from Madura island off Java reportedly stabbed two native Borneo Dayak tribesmen.

This came less than a week after a mob of mainly Moslem youths set shops, buildings and some churches ablaze in Tasikmalaya, West Java, apparently incensed by alleged police brutality towards some Moslem religious teachers.
In his New Year address, President Suharto called for tolerance and unity and pledged more openness and democracy.
